newsitem.title: UK: UK banks reverse early gains amid profit taking.
newsitem.headline: UK banks reverse early gains amid profit taking.

text.p: Shares in Britain's banking sector reversed their early gains on Monday after a strong bull run, fired by the Halifax Plc flotation, encouraged profit-taking, said analysts.
"The sector has shown a strong performance and there are now those who think it is time to take profits," said Nick Collier, analyst at Morgan Stanley.
Abbey National shares fell back 21p to 858, Barclays Plc dropped 40-1/2p to 1147p while Lloyds TSB Group declined 23p to 592.

"We have obviously had a technical squeeze for quite a while and slightly weak economic data this morning, which has weakened the gilt market, plus worries of a base rate rise at the end of the week are all excuses for taking profits. The shares have had a huge run," said Phil Pickard, analyst at HSBC James Capel.

Dealers said the sudden reversal in bank stocks had been on the cards as Halifax made its long-awaited market debut. Institutions had been accumulating other bank stocks in the run-up to the float, partly as a proxy for the new heavily-weighted stock.
"I suspect there has been selling of some banking shares to pay for Halifax stock," said one.
Meanwhile economists argued a raft of economic data showing Britain's manufacturers perking up while consumer demand remains robust raised the likelihood of an interest rate rise this week.
Higher interest rates act to discourage borrowing, thereby affecting the banks' main business, as well as tending to narrow the margin between lending and borrowing rates.
Some brokers have recently turned more cautious on the financial services sector and reduced their weightings.
Strategists at Goldman Sachs, for instance, on Friday cut their recommended weighting on the sector to "underweight" from "neutral."

Other analysts said the spread of 710p to 815p per share achieved at the Halifax auction of around 570 million shares this morning, showed that some institutions were holding too much at too high a price in the short term.
Halifax shares opened trading at 774-1/2p before falling back to 745p by 1018 GMT.
